environmental-science--carrying-capacity.title: logistic growth and the carrying capacity
environmental-science--carrying-capacity.note: Growth is near-exponential while N is far below K and stalls as N approaches K, giving the S-shaped curve.

environmental-science--acid-rain.title: why clean rain sits at pH 5.6
symbols: first dissociation constant of carbonic acid
environmental-science--acid-rain.note: Rain more acidic than pH 5.6 must carry another acid, normally sulphuric or nitric from SOx and NOx.

environmental-science--greenhouse-effect.title: radiative forcing to equilibrium warming
environmental-science--greenhouse-effect.note: The logarithmic form comes from saturated CO2 absorption bands, and lambda folds in water-vapour and ice-albedo feedbacks.

environmental-science--noise-pollution.title: sound levels and their effects
environmental-science--noise-pollution.note: Each 10 dB step is ten times the sound intensity, so the 8-hour limit at 85 dB falls to minutes near 110 dB.

environmental-science--ozone-layer-deple.title: ozone depletion potentials
environmental-science--ozone-layer-deple.note: ODP is referenced to CFC-11 equal to 1; bromine is roughly 45 times more destructive per atom than chlorine.
